name: Wilhelminapark
title: Ancient Trees in Wilhelminapark, Breda: 5 Worth Finding
meta_description: Leonard Springer laid out this Breda park in 1894 around a lime already decades old: five registered trees, an 1860s lime to a catalpa propped on the pond.
intro: Leonard Springer laid out the Wilhelminapark in 1894, and its oldest tree already stood on that ground for thirty years before he arrived: a silver lime from the 1860s, its leaves felted silver underneath, planted near what is now a stone bench positioned to sit beneath it. Springer's own park brought the rest, all dated by the Dutch national monument register to the 1890s: a weeping beech at the pond's western edge whose lowest branches root back into the soil, a Caucasian wingnut on the Vijverstraat corner that strings its seeds in half-metre chains, and a plain green beech along Paul Withausenweg standing quietly among its more colourful, copper and weeping cousins. The fifth tree breaks from the register's dating entirely: a catalpa leaning so far out over the pond that the municipality now props its lowest limbs on columns, its age inferred from the park's own founding rather than any planting record. All five stand within a few minutes' walk of each other, free and open daily.
